peer_results.rationale: BAC's candidate disclosures relate to MLPF&S regulatory net capital (bac_2024_7_D195) and Net DVA accounting (bac_2024_7_D116). Although MLPF&S provides 'retail services' (bac_2024_7_P217_S001), the disclosure concerns regulatory capital compliance for an investment banking/wholesale entity, not the FICO score distribution or consumer credit quality metrics central to C's Retail Services portfolio analysis. The topic of consumer FICO scores is absent.

comparisons.peer_summary: The risk assessment process may include reviewing key metrics such as delinquency status, collateral value, FICO credit scores, and other risk factors where applicable.
comparisons.comparison: While C explicitly reports on the stability and quality of its U.S. Retail Services portfolio FICO distribution, GS describes its internal risk assessment process. GS states that its risk assessment process 'may also include, where applicable, reviewing certain key metrics, including, but not limited to, delinquency status, collateral value, FICO credit scores' (gs_2024_7_P415_S001). Unlike C, which presents FICO data as an outcome reflecting credit quality, GS outlines FICO scores as an input variable in its broader risk assessment methodology for various portfolios.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risk Factors for Wholesale and Consumer Loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Risk factors for wholesale loans include credit ratings, industry data, macroeconomic indicators, and collateral metrics, while installment and credit card loans consider FICO scores, delinquency status, and vintage.
comparisons.comparison: This GS disclosure explicitly lists 'Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) credit scores' as a risk factor for installment and credit card loans, alongside delinquency status and loan vintage (gs_2024_7_P026_S010). This relates to C's disclosure, which analyzes the FICO distribution of its Retail Services portfolio to reflect underlying credit quality. Both disclosures identify FICO scores as a critical metric for evaluating consumer credit risk, though GS defines it as a forward-looking risk factor for forecasting while C presents it as a descriptive statistic of current portfolio quality.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Loan Quality and Collateralization
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, more than 75% of Wealth Management residential real estate loans were extended to borrowers with 'Exceptional' or 'Very Good' FICO scores exceeding 740, and the securities-based lending portfolio remains well-collateralized subject to daily client margining.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and MS disclose specific FICO score quality metrics for distinct consumer lending portfolios. C reports that its U.S. Retail Services portfolio FICO distribution was 'broadly stable quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year' reflecting 'strong underlying credit quality' (c_2024_7_P335_S001, c_2024_7_P335_S002). Similarly, MS reports that for its Wealth Management residential real estate loans, 'more than 75%... were to borrowers with "Exceptional" or "Very Good" FICO scores (i.e., exceeding 740)' as of year-end 2024 (ms_2024_7_P361_S001). Both disclosures use FICO scores to substantiate the credit quality of their respective consumer-facing portfolios, although C emphasizes stability over time while MS emphasizes the high percentage of high-score borrowers at a specific point in time.
